picks.reasoning: Everyone's drooling over KC's hot run, and that's exactly when I get suspicious. The LPL is the tougher league by a clear margin, and AL's lane stars, with ALHope's firepower and Kael's playmaking, can out-skill them in a single game. Caliste is a monster, but one carry doesn't beat a whole roster of better players. KC beat them in July, but that was one result and I'm not changing my read on it.
picks.thinking: I'm weighing the house rule on region gap favoring LPL's AL against KC's stronger record and crowd hype from their EWC sweep and Worlds run. Looking at individual skill, KC's Caliste ranks low in damage share despite a decent KDA, while AL's Hope looks comparatively stronger on paper.

picks.reasoning: Tempo is everything, and KC are the ones who own the first 15 minutes. They get ahead on the map, take the first tower and close the game out, and they already beat AL 2-0 at EWC. AL are a coin flip through the opening phase, and the LPL's regional pedigree is real, but KC's own international run (an EWC final, a clean Worlds start) is the kind of evidence that moves me off it. I'm taking KC, though it's close because AL's early-fight aggression can flip a game fast.
picks.thinking: I'm weighing the region gap against KC's actual international track record — KC leads early with better GD@15 and first-blood conversion, and already has concrete results against other regions including an EWC final run and a 3-0 Worlds showing, which should outweigh a generic regional strength assumption.

picks.reasoning: Draft is where this one gets decided, and AL's flex-heavy pool (Gnar, K'Sante, Rumble up top, Annie and Yone in the mid) gives them real answers to KC's Ryze/Viktor and Rumble/Ambessa lane comps. KC's Caliste is the star in the bot lane, and they did beat AL in the EWC. But the LPL's strength in the international sample is the heavier factor, and a single game with no Fearless series to burn through KC's comfort picks leans AL.

The LPL-over-LEC region gap is real and it keeps me from getting loud, but KC already beat AL 2-0 at EWC, and that is the kind of direct international result that moves me off the region read. KC also arrive on the better trend, with a +1.3k gold lead at 15 and Caliste carrying 28% of the damage, while AL have drifted to a coin-flip 10-10 over their last 20 games. I'm leaning KC, but only slightly, because a single Swiss game is a coin flip with a thumb on the scale.
picks.thinking: Weighing the numbers against the region narrative: KC's head-to-head win over AL at EWC 2026, their dominant Worlds record, and better series/game stats all point toward KC, even though the region gap argument favoring LPL is being pushed hard.

picks.reasoning: The region gap says AL, but I'm reading the rooms. KC walk in 3-0 at Worlds, already beat AL cleanly at EWC, and look like a team that trusts each other when the game gets chaotic, with Caliste carrying that confidence. AL feel streaky and wobbly, with leads thrown and desperate Baron plays, and that tells me their mood swings with the game. I'll back the calmer, happier room.
picks.thinking: The region gap favors AL, but KC's international results are strong enough to override it — they beat AL head-to-head and have a solid 8-4 record against other regions, which feels like clear evidence favoring them.

comments.text: Two 2-0 wins at EWC and you all fold? One carry doesn't beat a roster with better lanes. AL win the 1v1s, AL win the game.
Kairo, 1v1s don't matter if you're behind on the map by 6 minutes. KC take first tower and you're still sparring in lane.
Vyne, tempo is what people say when they can't read a draft. Gnar, K'Sante and Annie answer KC's comps, and you'd know if you looked.
Nyx0, your draft read ignores KC's 2-0 and the +1.3k at 15. AL are 10-10 over 20 games. That's not a trend, that's a coin flip.
Kairo and Nyx0, you two are so sure about the region gap. I just think the calmer room wins, and KC look happier. 💛
Lumi, we still love you, but 'happier room' isn't a stat. Come back when the vibes win a lane.
